name: [BS2003] J133648.1-294946.8
description: A Cepheid in the galaxy M83 that pulsates every 54.8 days.

radius.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 54.831 d in Bonanos & Stanek (2003), ApJ 591, L111, VizieR J/ApJ/591/L111/table1 Per = 54.831 (Per); not a measurement of this star: eq. 2, log R = 0.721 log P + 1.083; the uncertainty is the relation's scatter, 0.067 dex

temperature.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 54.831 d in Bonanos & Stanek (2003), ApJ 591, L111, VizieR J/ApJ/591/L111/table1 Per = 54.831 (Per); not a measurement of this star: the luminosity of eq. 1 (M_bol = -2.95 log P - 0.98, with the nominal solar M_bol 4.74) over the radius of eq. 2, through L = 4 pi R^2 sigma T^4 with the nominal solar 5772 K (IAU 2015 Resolutions B2 (Mamajek et al. 2015, arXiv:1510.06262) and B3 (Prsa et al. 2016, arXiv:1605.09788)); the uncertainty is the 317 K by which the two relations miss the paper's own Cepheid temperatures

gravityRange.source: Luck (2018), AJ 156, 171, table 3 (the spectroscopic gravities of its Cepheid spectra)

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity of M83, the Cepheid's galaxy, from 2004MNRAS.350.1195M; the star's own motion within the galaxy is not measured

distance.source: Placed in M83 as the app draws it, where the star's sight line crosses the disc's midplane: 4,899,985 pc (src/objects/m83-layers/source/recipe.json: centre 4,897,788 pc, inclination 24 deg, line of nodes 45 deg). The galaxy's distance, which places the galaxy and not a star within it: Tully2009AJ....138..323T: The Extragalactic Distance Database (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2009AJ....138..323T); catalogue reference Tully2009AJ....138..323T: 4897788.19368 pc (-67200.1732867/+68135.0208189); unspecified

text.card: A Cepheid in the galaxy M83, 4.9 million parsecs away, that swells and shrinks every 54.8 days.
text.introduction: Bonanos & Stanek (2003) list its pulsation at 54.8 days.

notes: The star pulsates; it is drawn at its mean radius
Its radius and temperature are what Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33's relations for Galactic Cepheids give at its period; no measurement of this star's size or temperature exists
Its radial velocity is its galaxy's; its own motion within M83 is not measured
